findings.title: README implies SSKR --output files have an MNC1 record header
findings.reproduction: Read the generic --output paragraph and invoke encode --sskr --mnemonic <published abandon/about vector> --threshold 2 --shares 3 --output <new path>.
findings.expected: The paragraph scopes MNC1 headers to ordinary non-SSKR encode records or explicitly distinguishes the SSKR share-file format.
findings.observed: README states any file written with --output starts with MNC1. Ordinary encode uses serializeRecord; integrated SSKR writes shares.join newline. The new SSKR output contains three ur:sskr lines and no MNC1 header. docs/SSKR.md correctly says one share per line.
findings.impact: Readers can mistake SSKR output for an MNC1 record and mishandle a recovery file; both formats remain recoverable when read according to their specific guide.
findings.evidence: AUD-006-evidence/sskr-output-format.log and sskr-output-shape.log (local); source lines 28 in encode-export.ts and 155 in sskr-command.ts; README.md:371; docs/SSKR.md:20.
findings.recommendedFix: State that ordinary non-SSKR encode --output writes an MNC1 record and link to the SSKR guide for --sskr output.
findings.requiredVerification: Text-only public-vector assertions for ordinary MNC1 output and SSKR UR output; confirm each documented format matches the production entry point.
